title: Anyone else experiencing massive GSC indexing drops, disappearing breadcrumbs, and reporting bugs since October 12, 2026?
summary: I'm wondering if anyone else is experiencing serious issues with Google Search Console around October 12–13, 2026. I manage a bilingual (German/French) website with roughly 300 URLs. Until October 11, the site was gaining visibility in Google Search, and several important pages were ranking and receiving organic clicks. Then, almost overnight, things changed dramatically. Here's what I'm seeing: Massive impression drop: Google Search Console reported 286 impressions on October 11, 125 on October 12, and only 9 on October 13. By October 15, impressions had dropped to zero. Breadcrumb rich results disappearing: The number of valid breadcrumb items in GSC dropped from approximately 27 to just 4, despite the structured data still being present and valid. Previously visible pages no longer indexed: Important product reviews, category hubs, and informational pages are now marked as "Crawled – currently not indexed." No obvious technical problems: Googlebot successfully crawls these pages, receives HTTP 200 responses, indexing is allowed, and Google recognizes the correct canonical URLs. Live URL tests pass: The live inspection confirms that pages can be indexed. Google renders the content correctly and recognizes valid breadcrumb structured data. Outdated indexing reports: As of October 20, my Page Indexing report was still showing October 12 as its last update. Sitemap inconsistencies: URL Inspection sometimes displays "Temporary processing error" or "No referring sitemaps detected," even though the URLs are included in submitted sitemaps. Broken date picker: When selecting a custom date range, GSC displayed bizarre validation messages referring to January 1, 1970, and June 20, 2025. Interestingly, Google Analytics 4 doesn't show a traffic decline anywhere near as severe as the impression drop reported by GSC. However, GA4 sessions and GSC clicks are different metrics, so I don't want to draw conclusions from that discrepancy alone. Both language homepages remain indexed, while multiple important internal pages in both languages are currently excluded. I've checked robots directives, canonicals, hreflang, XML sitemaps, server responses, rendering, and structured data. I haven't found a sitewide technical issue that explains such a sudden change. There are also no manual actions or security issues reported in Search Console. My questions: Has anyone experienced a similar sudden drop in impressions or indexed pages around October 12–13? Are your Page Indexing and Breadcrumb reports updating normally? Has anyone encountered the same broken date picker or temporary sitemap processing errors? Could this be related to a Google indexing/reporting issue, or have you seen similar behavior following a major algorithm update? I'm not claiming this is definitely a Google bug. I'm trying to determine whether this is an isolated website issue or whether other site owners are seeing the same pattern. Any experiences or insights would be greatly appreciated. Michael   submitted by   /u/Silberzwiebel [link]   [comments]

title: What would you say are the main differences between local SEO, B2B SEO (manufacturing, industrial, wholesale, etc.), SaaS SEO, and ecommerce SEO? And is it possible to jump from one type to another?
summary: I'm interested in understanding how the actual SEO work differs between these specializations. Obviously, the fundamentals overlap, but I'd imagine there are meaningful differences in the strategies, technical challenges, and day-to-day tasks involved. For example, my understanding is that the work might look something like this: Local SEO: Google Business Profile optimization, local landing pages, citation management, review management, local link building, and location-based keyword research. B2B SEO (manufacturing, industrial, wholesale, etc.): Optimizing product and application pages, keyword research around technical products and industry terminology, improving site architecture, technical SEO, and creating content around specific products, materials, specifications, and use cases. SaaS SEO: Programmatic SEO, comparison and alternative pages, feature and use-case pages, content hubs, product-led content, and managing indexation for large numbers of URLs. Ecommerce SEO: Product and category page optimization, faceted navigation, handling duplicate and thin pages, structured data, internal linking, crawl budget management, and large-scale product catalog optimization. For those who have worked across multiple specializations: What are the biggest differences in the actual work you do day to day? Which areas require the most specialized knowledge or have the steepest learning curve? How transferable are the skills between these specializations? For example, how difficult would it be for someone experienced in local or B2B SEO to transition into SaaS or ecommerce SEO? Are there any specializations where experience in another area gives you a significant advantage, or where the learning curve is particularly steep? I'd especially like to hear from people who have worked in two or more of these areas and can compare their experiences firsthand.   submitted by   /u/doorstoinfinity [link]   [comments]
